findings.title: enableSqlExpressions contains dead/misleading logic that always returns false
findings.body: The new helper always returns false regardless of the feature flag value: `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`; `if enabled { return false }`; `return false`. Both branches return the same literal, so the computed `enabled` value (and the feature-flag lookup itself) is completely unused/irrelevant, and the variable name `enabled` is also inverted relative to what it actually measures (it is true when the flag is NOT enabled). This makes the code highly misleading: a future maintainer could easily believe toggling `FlagSqlExpressions` re-enables SQL expressions, when in fact it never will with this implementation, and there's no comment explaining that this is an intentional, hard-coded kill-switch for a security fix (CVE-2024-9264). This should be simplified to an explicit `return false` with a clear comment, to avoid confusion and accidental 'fixes' that re-enable the vulnerable code path.

findings.title: No test coverage added for disabling SQL expressions
findings.body: This PR's core behavior change is that QueryTypeSQL now always errors out with "sqlExpressions is not implemented" via enableSqlExpressions(), which is the security-relevant fix. No test changes are included in the diff to verify this behavior (e.g., a test that ReadQuery returns an error for QueryTypeSQL regardless of feature flag state), nor are there tests for the new pkg/expr/sql/db.go stub (DB.TablesList/RunCommands/QueryFramesInto) to confirm they always fail safely. Given the severity of the vulnerability being fixed, a regression test preventing silent re-enablement of SQL expression execution is important and currently missing.

findings.title: Misleading public error message when SQL expressions are effectively disabled
findings.body: NewSQLCommand calls sql.TablesList(rawSQL), which now always fails because pkg/expr/sql/db.go's DB.RunCommands is a stub that unconditionally returns errors.New("not implemented"). When this happens, NewSQLCommand returns errutil.BadRequest("sql-invalid-sql", errutil.WithPublicMessage("error reading SQL command")), which tells the user their SQL is invalid, when the real reason is that the feature has been completely disabled/stubbed out. Any code path that reaches NewSQLCommand without going through ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery's explicit "sqlExpressions is not implemented" check (e.g. UnmarshalSQLCommand, used for raw-node parsing) will surface this confusing message instead of a clear explanation, making it harder for users/admins to diagnose why previously working SQL expressions now fail.

findings.title: Leftover DuckDB-specific code/naming contradicts stated PR goal of removing DuckDB references
findings.body: The PR description states the intent is to "Remove reference to DuckDB", but TablesList still names its local variable `duckDB` (`duckDB := NewInMemoryDB()`) and still constructs a DuckDB-specific SQL command (`SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')`) to pass to RunCommands, even though the underlying DB is now a stub that always returns "not implemented" and has nothing to do with DuckDB. This leftover naming/logic is confusing: it implies the code still talks to a DuckDB engine with a real SQL dialect, when in fact it is now dead code whose output is always discarded due to the stub's unconditional error. This should be cleaned up or at minimum commented to reflect that the underlying engine has been removed.
